references.text: The angel of the Lord calls to Abraham from heaven, and he answers 'Here I am' (הִנֵּנִי) – the same pattern as when God's angel calls to Jacob in a dream.
Jacob has a dream at Bethel where God speaks to him and gives him promises – this mirrors how God's angel speaks to Jacob in a dream in Gen 31:11.
The angel identifies himself as the God of Bethel and links the dream back to Jacob's experience in Gen 28.
Jacob meets God's angels on his journey, reflecting his repeated encounters with God's angel in dreams and visions.
God speaks to Israel in a night vision and calls 'Jacob, Jacob!', and he answers 'Here I am' (הִנֵּנִי) – a close parallel to Gen 31:11.
Hosea refers to Jacob's struggle with the angel and his meeting with God, illuminating Jacob's repeated revelations from God's angels.
Complementary scenes in Jacob's life where God's revelation in dreams leads to recognition of His holy presence.
A clear theological parallel in the prophetic call structure (name-call-response) that illustrates how God initiates His mission with His servants.
A strong theological parallel in the response to God's call ('Here I am'), highlighting the prophetic pattern of attentiveness and willingness.
